title: Micro-decision log: greeting vs signature split
content:
Purpose:
This is a micro-decision log for how we separate greetings and signatures from main message content for the informal messaging dataset. Keeping this lightweight — quick rules, examples, and unresolved items for reviewers. Goal is to reduce labeler ambiguity and downstream model hallucination when prompts use message body only for generation/eval.

High-level proposal (working):
- GreetSpan: explicit opening salutations ("Hi", "Hello team", "Dear Sarah", localized variants). Usually the first contiguous short span at the top of a message.
- SignSpan: explicit closing phrases and tokens indicating author identity/contact info ("Thanks,", "Best, Anton", phone numbers, titles on separate lines).
- Body: everything else. If a greeting or signature is fused inline (not separated by newline), prefer including in Body unless a clear delimiter (comma + newline or line break).

Why this matters:
- Downstream fine-tuning: prompts that include greetings/signatures change style distribution; we want to optionally strip them.
- Extraction tasks: entity parsers should not treat signatures as part of core request content.
- Evaluation: presence of greeting/signature affects perplexity / token counts — remove when analyzing core semantics.

Concrete heuristics (quick, labeler-facing):
1) Top-of-message rule: if a sequence of tokens at the start matches common greeting tokens and is < 6 tokens long, mark as GreetSpan unless immediately followed by sentence content (no linebreak) and the phrase is part of a larger clause (e.g., "Hi there I wanted to ask...").
2) Trailing-line rule: if final 1-4 lines are short (< 16 tokens per line) and contain names, salutations, canonical closers (thanks, regards), emails, phone numbers, mark as SignSpan.
3) Inline exception: if greeting appears mid-paragraph as part of an example or quoted text, label as Body.
4) Name-only lines: single-word final-line names are SignSpan ("Anton"). If ambiguous (e.g., 'Monday' as single final line), mark as Body and add note tag for adjudication.
5) Signature blocks with contact blocks (email, phone, company) are always SignSpan even if long.

Examples (label -> span):
- "Hi Eve, can you send the report?
Thanks,
Marco" -> GreetSpan: "Hi Eve,"; Body: "can you send the report?"; SignSpan: "Thanks,
Marco"
- "Hello team we need to..." (no newline) -> GreetSpan? NO. Labeler note: treat as Body unless punctuation or newline separates greeting.
- "Quick note: Thanks everyone for the review" -> SignSpan? NO. Here "Thanks" is inline; treat as Body.
- "Dear Dr. Huang:
I'm following up..." -> GreetSpan: "Dear Dr. Huang:"
- "Hey — saw this and forwarded" -> Body (em dash attaches it)
- "Cheers
S." -> SignSpan: "Cheers
S."
- "Bonjour, je vous envoie..." -> GreetSpan: supports localized tokens (French/Spanish/Portuguese greetings). Add localization checklist below.

Localization notes:
- Maintain short lookup table for common openers in major languages: en, fr, es, pt, de, zh-basic variants. Keep conservative: if unknown, default to Body.
- Non-Latin scripts: rely on linebreak and punctuation heuristics more than token lookup.

Ambiguous/edge cases (for adjudication):
- Single-line messages where the whole message is "Thanks" or "Thanks!" — should be SignSpan-only (the message intent is closing). But often these are conversational acknowledgements and could be Body for intent detection tasks. Mark for reviewer if downstream use is unclear.
- Email-like footers that are not author signatures but forwarded reply chain ("On Tue ... wrote:") — mark as Body unless clear signature block after the chain.
- Chat transcripts: people often prefix with names ("Marcy: I'll do it") — treat speaker labels as Body unless separated into a signature block.

Labeler checklist (quick):
- Is there a newline after the first short phrase? If yes and greeting tokens, GreetSpan.
- Are the last few lines small and name/email/closing-word heavy? If yes, SignSpan.
- If uncertain, add tag "needs-adjudication" and copy 2 similar examples into the adjudication doc.

Impact experiments to run (notes):
- A/B strip greetings for downstream NLU intent classification and compare F1. Hypothesis: neutral effect for intents, lowers token variance.
- Measure model generation politeness when prompts include vs exclude greeting/signature.

Open decisions and TODOs:
- [ ] Build small regex + token list for multi-lang greetings (Sophie to prototype).
- [ ] Decide canonical adjudication guideline for single-token messages like "Thanks" (design leads).
- [ ] Add a "signature-entity" label type for structured extraction of phone/email when present (Marco owns the POC).
- [ ] Example set of 200 borderline messages to send to labeling pool for calibration (I will compile).

Quick pseudo-rule summary for labelers (one-liners):
- If at top and short + newline -> GreetSpan.
- If last chunk is short and contains closers/names/contacts -> SignSpan.
- Inline or grammatical integration -> Body.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc short; move finalized rules to Confluence after first 2 rounds of adjudication.
- Track how many "needs-adjudication" flags per week; target < 2% after training.

Recent examples I flagged for adjudication (copy-paste):
1) "Thanks so much for the quick turnaround." (single line) -> flagged (S1)
2) "Ok will do. — Sam" -> flagged (S2)
3) "Hi all pls review and confirm
John" -> clear Greet+Sign but sometimes John is part of inline quote; keep note.

References and links:
- See linked PR for prototype scripts that detect candidate spans (linked_artifacts above).
- Related ticket JIRA-2341: add signature entity extraction.

End of micro-log. Keep this as ephemeral working doc.
